title: Managed Identity with Storage
description: Use managed identities to authenticate to Azure Blob Storage, Queue Storage, and Table Storage without keys.

data.text: Storage account keys give full access to the entire storage account. If a key leaks, an attacker can read, modify, or delete data. Managed identities let you grant granular access to specific containers or queues.
Azure Storage supports Entra ID authentication for Blob, Queue, and Table endpoints. You can use RBAC or Azure AD workload identity to control access.

data.title: Storage Permissions via RBAC
items: Storage Blob Data Reader — read blobs and containers
Storage Blob Data Contributor — read, write, delete blobs
Storage Queue Data Contributor — send and receive queue messages
Storage Table Data Contributor — manage table entities

data.title: Assign Storage Blob Data Role with Azure CLI
data.content: Give a managed identity permission to read blobs in a specific storage account.
data.code: az role assignment create   --assignee "managed-identity-principal-id"   --role "Storage Blob Data Reader"   --scope "/subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/myStorage"

data.title: Upload a Blob Using Managed Identity (C#)
data.content: Authenticate to Blob Storage with DefaultAzureCredential and upload a file.

data.text: Storage accounts are protected by two independent planes. The control plane uses Azure Resource Manager and Azure RBAC. The data plane uses the blob, queue, table, or file endpoint and accepts either a shared key, a SAS token, or an Entra ID token. A managed identity uses the data plane, so the role must be a data role such as Storage Blob Data Reader or Storage Blob Data Contributor.

data.title: Disable shared key access and use Entra ID
data.content: Disabling shared keys forces every caller to use Entra ID or a user delegation SAS, which removes the account-wide master key from your threat model.
data.code:
az storage account update -g rg-shop -n shopstorage --allow-shared-key-access false

principalId=$(az webapp identity show -g rg-shop -n shop-api --query principalId -o tsv)

# Scope to a single container instead of the whole account
containerId=$(az storage container show --account-name shopstorage --name invoices \
  --auth-mode login --query id -o tsv)

az role assignment create \
  --assignee-object-id "$principalId" \
  --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "Storage Blob Data Contributor" \
  --scope "$containerId"

data.text: The BlobServiceClient constructor accepts a TokenCredential. Because the service URI has no key or SAS, every request is signed with an Entra ID token. Use the account endpoint without a container name, and create container clients from it.

data.title: Upload a blob with DefaultAzureCredential
data.content: The same code works locally with your developer sign-in and in Azure with the managed identity.

data.title: Azurite and local emulators do not support managed identity
data.text: Local emulators use a fixed account and key. Keep a development-only connection string behind a configuration switch, and make sure the production path never falls back to it.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: If asked how to secure blob access, lead with "disable shared key access and use Entra ID data-plane roles". Then mention user delegation SAS for time-limited external sharing, private endpoints for network isolation, and the fact that Contributor alone cannot read blob data.

data.title: Secure a Storage Container
data.description: Disable storage account keys, enable Entra ID authentication, and verify your managed identity can read a blob.
steps: Create a storage account and a container named 'secure-data'.
Enable 'Azure Storage keyvault secrets' or use RBAC to grant access.
Assign Storage Blob Data Reader to your managed identity.
data.expectedOutcome: Your app can read blobs using managed identity even though the storage key is disabled.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Storage keys provide full access — avoid them when possible.
RBAC roles like Storage Blob Data Reader give granular control.
